text:
michael: Heads-up — noticed an odd pattern this morning: GPUs in warm-pool were scaled down during a 3min quiet window even though pods were queued with cold-start label.
anya: wait what, warm-pool should prevent that. any logs? :thinking_face:
kevin: saw the same in eu-west. autoscaler metrics show nodeUnneeded but warmPoolSize > 0.
sre-oncall: @autoscaler-bot can you paste the last scale decision for cluster-prod-eu?
autoscaler-bot: decision: scaleDownCandidates=[nodepool-eu-gpu-7], reason=utilization<0.12, lastProbe=2027-11-24T08:31:10Z, scaleDownUnneededTime=300s
michael: config snippet for the pool (from terraform):
```hcl
resource "redwood_node_pool" "gpu-eu" {
  name = "gpu-eu"
  warm_pool = true
  warm_pool_min_size = 2
  scale_down_unneeded_time = 300
  scale_down_unready_time = 600
}
```
anya: hm config seems fine. are these nodes annotated `k8s.io/cluster-autoscaler/excludenode`?
kevin: double-checked — warm pool nodes have annotation but some transient nodes don't. I suspect the probe jitter made the autoscaler think warm pool was empty for a short epoch.
michael: we saw a burst of kubelet reconnects at 08:31 — network flakiness in the AZ. Kube-controller flagged nodes NotReady for ~20s then back. autoscaler uses consecutive probes, so it flagged nodes as unneeded and removed one.
sre-oncall: consequence: ~2s of cold-start increased P99 for inference by 1.2s for a small set of requests. Not a major outage but measurable.
anya: ideas: increase `scale_down_unneeded_time` for gpu pools? or add a `quiet_window` to avoid scaling during reconnections?
kevin: we could add a short holdback loop: don't scale-down if warm_pool_min_size would drop below current warm cache hit rate threshold. Need a metric for cache warm hits.
michael: sketch: add a small policy in autoscaler that checks prefix cache hits (kvcache_hits/min) and defers scale when below threshold. Also, bump `scale_down_unneeded_time` to 10m for gpu pools by default.
anya: action items: 1) increase scale_down_unneeded_time in staging to 10m and observe for 48h, 2) add metric export for kvcache hits per node, 3) create an autoscaler PR to consult warm-pool annotations before final decision.
sre-oncall: filing a quick incident note in #incidents and tagging infra-ops.
kevin: will open the PR. putting a draft config change now.
michael: thanks — also add a tracking todo to avoid similar effects for Dedicated pools in us-west (different AZ flakiness).
anya: ack. will run a small canary tomorrow morning during low traffic. :thumbsup:
